evidence: The Thread of Ice party topped out at the Eye Col and finished with 'a bit of 5.7 rock'. The North Buttress party scrambled the summit block 'at perhaps 5.6' and downclimbed and rapped to the Eye Col. Beckey (as quoted) singles out East Twin Needle as the one cirque peak harder than low fifth class.
note: No source names a grade for the South Route itself. The 5.7 rock is reported at the top of the couloir that leads to the Eye Col and is not explicitly placed on the East summit block. The 2003 enchainment's 'southeast ridge/face, II 5.10a' line is a different, harder route.

evidence: First-ascent account: 300 ft of 'grade III climbing (a few pitons)', then a 300-ft 50-degree ice patch, then 600 ft of steep but easier upslab rock. It calls the ice the main difficulty. No modern grade exists.
note: 50-degree ice maps to roughly AI2; the record's ice_grade AI3 is unsourced. The 1961 'grade III' is in an old numeral system (the same author wrote 'class V' for roped 5th class), so the rock may be low 5th; if it proves 5th class, re-grade on yds. The record's 'Class 3-4' rock_grade belongs to the NE Ledge traverse, not to this face.
identity: The record merges two routes: Cooper and Ferguson's 1961 direct Northeast Face (rock plus a 50-degree ice patch), and the 'NE Ledge AKA Northeast Face', the old normal route, which is a Class 3-4 traverse below the east ridge (the AAJ editor's note and SummitPost both say so).

evidence: From the Fortress-Chiwawa col: 'a gully of loose rock, class 3 some 4' onto the ridge, then an exposed '4th class step' to the summit (2020 TR). Other reports cite a 4th-class chimney on the northeast ridge.
note: No source describes the roped headwall pitches in the overview. Every documented line on this side tops out at Class 4.
identity: The id says northeast_face and the overview describes a pitched rock headwall plus a snow face, but the route name and breakdown describe the Northeast/East Ridge scramble from the Fortress-Chiwawa saddle, which is the line the sources document.

evidence: 2003 Complete Southern Pickets Traverse summary: 'Frenzlespitz, southeast ridge/face, II 5.6'. The 1961 first-ascent account gives the approach (about 500 ft down Ottohorn's north face) but no grade.
note: Both AAJ entries come from the same 2003 party, so they are one source, not two. They confirm commitment II, which settles the record's III-vs-II conflict in favour of II. No source supports the '5.7ish' aside in rock_grade.

evidence: SummitPost South Route (Difficulty 'Class 4/5'): #2 Gully has 'steps of varying difficulty ranging from Class 3 to Class 5.8', partly 'low 5th Class rock (unprotectable)'. A cascadeclimber.com TR describes 'five pitches of loose, unprotectable fifth-class rock to the summit', belayed off a fixed ring piton.

fix.rock_grade: Low to mid 5th class in #2 Gully (loose, poorly protected)

note: Calling this a Class 4 scramble is contradicted by every source: the main summit needs roped fifth-class climbing in #2 Gully. 5.8 is one party's hardest step on a gully with many variations, so confidence is low.
identity: This 'Multi-Summit Scramble' row describes the same South Route on the Main Peak as wa_garfield_mountain_south_route (same face, first ascent and landmarks), so it is a duplicate.

evidence: SummitPost South Route: #2 Gully 'steps of varying difficulty ranging from Class 3 to Class 5.8'; crux was 'a short climb of 15 feet between slab and overhang'. A cascadeclimber TR describes several loose fifth-class pitches; Beckey's optional Chimney Variation is 'two leads easy class 5'.

fix.rock_grade: Up to 5.8 in #2 Gully (mostly low 5th, loose and poorly protected)

note: SummitPost is the only source that gives a number. The record's 5.4 is unsourced. The gully has many variations, so an easier line may top out lower.

evidence: First-ascent report (AAJ 1971): the route was 'from the notch south of the peak which was gained from the west', on the south and west sides, and 'involved easy to moderate fifth-class pitches'. Wikipedia lists the easiest route as Class 4.
note: The route-specific first-ascent source says roped fifth class, so the record's 'Class 4' headline is too low. No number is published; 5.0 is the brief's no-number default, and 'moderate' suggests the crux may be harder (around 5.4-5.6).

evidence: SummitPost (route difficulty 'Moderate'): bergschrund, a '40degree headwall', then a 'steep 45degree slope (often icy) about 180 ft'. Gear listed: rope, pickets, 4 ice screws.
note: Steep, often-icy snow protected with screws and pickets, with no published ice grade, maps to Class 3. The record's 'roughly AI1 when icy' is consistent with this, though unsourced; on the neighbouring Frostbite route, Mountain Project gives AI1-2 / Steep Snow.

evidence: First ascent on July 27, 1958 by Beckey and Watson 'from the Methow River' (confirmed by NWMJ and AAJ 2016). No grade, pitch count or description is published in any source found.
note: Searches tried: Golden Horn north face with Beckey/Watson/1958; north face/side with 5.x and class terms; AAJ 1959; Mountain Project, SummitPost (has no North Face route page), Wikipedia, NWMJ. The summit horn reached by the Southwest Route is low 5th, so any line here is at least that, but no source grades the north face. Left ungraded.

evidence: SummitPost North Ridge route page: 'Difficulty: 5.7+ Grade III', seven pitches from the deep notch north of the peak. A 2013 SummitPost TR describes the same seven pitches (friable P1, steep cracks, wide chimney, exposed west-side traverse).
note: The record has 5.7 with no commitment; the route page gives 5.7+ and Grade III.
identity: The id says southwest_slopes, but the row is the North Ridge from the north notch.

evidence: 1961 first ascent: a ledge from the west notch leads onto the north face, giving 'a class IV route'. Beckey (quoted in a 2017 NWHikers TR) calls it 'mainly class 4 with one lead of moderate class 5'. That party found it harder than Beckey describes. Wikipedia: YDS 5.
note: No number is published for the Firey/standard north-side route. 5.0 is the brief's no-number default, but 'moderate class 5', plus the 2017 party finding it harder than Beckey says, suggests the crux is likely 5.4-5.6. The record's commitment IV looks high: the 2003 party rated a harder Himmelhorn line II. Wild Hair Crack (5.7, 4 pitches) is a separate west-face route.
identity: The id says southeast_route, but the standard route goes from the Himmel-Otto (west) col onto the north/northwest face, which is what the face column says.

evidence: 2017 TR from the south saddle along the ridge between the summits: 'often-rotten class 4-5.easy scrambling', then 'a straightforward third class scramble' up the summit's southeast face. SummitPost: the easiest route on the North Peak is the class 4 NE face.
note: The party scrambled it unroped. Brief caps unroped scrambling at Class 4; a few steps may reach easy 5th.

evidence: Mountain Project's Sean's Route (5.8+), a variation of the 1983 Hardee-Coffey Northwest Buttress, says the original line turns left onto the lichen-covered ledge after pitch 1, and that the shared upper buttress is 'class 4-low fifth' to the false summit. No grade for the 1983 line is published.
note: 'Low 5th' with no number maps to 5.0. The 2021 variation's 5.8+ roof is not on the original line.

evidence: Trip report on this exact line (South Defile, South Gully, East Ridge): a steep snow finger and gully with deep moats, then the summit is a 'fun Class 2-3 scramble on solid pillow basalt'. No rope used.
note: Only the record's own breakdown says Class 3-4. The record's beta itself says 'a final pitch of Class 3 rock'. The steep, moated snow maps to Class 3.
